cards.text: King Asa of Judah is gone, and his son Jehoshaphat reigns in his place. Say JEHOSHAPHAT three times fast and your tongue's gonna need a nap. The new king gets to work and strengthens himself against Israel, the kingdom up north.

cards.question: How does the new king Jehoshaphat strengthen Judah against Israel?

answers.text: He stations troops in every fortified city
He sends silver to the king of Aram

cards.question: Jehoshaphat also puts garrisons in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.

cards.text: Troops in every fortified city? Nice. But here's the line that beats ALL of it, friend: the LORD is with Jehoshaphat.

cards.question: The LORD is with King Jehoshaphat. Why?

answers.text: He walked in the earlier ways of David
He brought gold back to the temple
He made his army the strongest around

cards.question: Jehoshaphat seeks the LORD, but he seeks the Baals too, just to cover his bases.
Jehoshaphat seeks the God of his father and walks by His commandments, not the practices of ___.

cards.text: So the LORD establishes the kingdom in Jehoshaphat's hand. Me, I spent years establishing myself in the back of a junk drawer, which is NOT the same thing.

cards.question: With the kingdom established, all Judah brings King Jehoshaphat tribute.

cards.text: Jehoshaphat ends up with an abundance of riches and honor, and his heart takes delight in the ways of the LORD. Rich, honored AND happy in the LORD? Somebody get this man a bigger cookie box.

cards.question: With his heart delighting in the LORD's ways, what does Jehoshaphat remove from Judah?

answers.text: The high places and Asherah poles
The golden calves of Bethel and Dan
The idols of Moab and Ammon

cards.text: In the third year of his reign, Jehoshaphat puts a team together: five officials, nine Levites and two priests. I'm not making you learn all sixteen names, friend, because one of them is Tob-adonijah and I'm STILL recovering from Jehoshaphat.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat sends his team of officials, Levites and priests out to ___ in the cities of Judah.
Jehoshaphat's team goes through all the towns of Judah. What do they carry with them?

answers.text: The Book of the Law of the LORD

cards.text: Then the dread of the LORD falls on all the kingdoms around Judah. Friend, I KNOW dread. Every time that junk drawer rattled open, everybody in there held their breath together, me included.

cards.question: Even with the dread of the LORD on them, the kingdoms around Judah still make war against Jehoshaphat.
Some Philistines bring Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute. What do the Arabs bring him?

answers.text: Rams and goats from their flocks

cards.question: Jehoshaphat grows stronger and stronger. In Judah he builds ___ and store cities.

cards.text: He keeps vast supplies in the cities of Judah, and in Jerusalem he's got mighty men of valor under five commanders from Judah and Benjamin. Add them up and it's over a million men, and that's besides the troops in the fortified cities. My favorite on the list is Amasiah son of Zichri, "the volunteer for the LORD," with 200,000 mighty men of valor. Nobody had to drag him in, he just raised his hand, and THAT'S my kind of baker. We'll pause here, friend, because Jehoshaphat's story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: The card reuses the troop placement from verse 2 (“Troops in every fortified city?”) but cites only verse 3. Its citation should begin with the first verse it uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: “Troops in every fortified city?”, “Nice.”, and the sentence about the LORD being with Jehoshaphat.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
